title: Bhutan for Indians: Permits, Documents and SDF
meta_description: Bhutan for Indians in 2026: passport or Voter ID, the free Entry Permit, route permits, ₹1,200 SDF a night, kids' rates and the licensed guide rule.
summary: Indians need no visa for Bhutan, but every visitor needs a free Entry Permit, shown with an Indian passport or original Voter ID. Aadhaar, PAN and driving licences are not accepted. Expect to pay the Sustainable Development Fee of ₹1,200 per person per night and plan on a licensed guide beyond Phuentsholing. Check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: No visa, but you still need a permit
paras: Indian citizens do not need a visa for Bhutan. What you do need is an Entry Permit, which is free and is issued by Bhutan's Department of Immigration. You can apply online in advance on the Immigration portal (visit.doi.gov.bt), or get it on arrival at the pedestrian terminal in Phuentsholing, opposite the Jaigaon gate, or at Paro airport. The smaller land crossings at Gelephu, Samdrup Jongkhar and Samtse also issue permits.

The Entry Permit lets you stay up to 15 days and covers Thimphu and Paro. If you need longer, the Immigration office in Thimphu can extend it. Most of our travellers are in Bhutan for five to eight nights, so 15 days is plenty. These rules have changed several times since Bhutan reopened in 2022, so check current status before you travel.

If you get the permit on arrival at Phuentsholing, go early. The Indian side, Jaigaon, is a busy market town, and the walk from your taxi to the gate takes 10 to 15 minutes through traffic. Inside the terminal, officers check your original document, your photos and your plan for each night. On a quiet weekday morning that can take 30 minutes; in peak October weeks it can take two hours. Your guide usually meets you on the Bhutan side of the gate and helps with the forms.

sections.heading: Documents that work and ones that do not
paras: This is where most Indian families get caught out. The Embassy of India in Thimphu lists only two documents for adults: an Indian passport valid for at least six months, or an original Voter ID card (EPIC). If you use a Voter ID, carry two or three passport-size photos as well. Photocopies and phone scans are not enough at the counter.

Aadhaar, PAN and driving licences are not accepted as travel documents, even though they are valid ID everywhere else in India. We have seen people turned back at Phuentsholing with only an Aadhaar card. Children under 18 who do not have a passport can travel on their original birth certificate.

sections.heading: Applying online, step by step
paras: Applying online saves an hour or more in the queue at Phuentsholing, especially on Saturdays in October and May. If you book through a Bhutanese tour operator, they usually file the application for you and send the permit by email. If you apply yourself, the process runs roughly like this.
list: Scan the photo page of your passport, or both sides of your original Voter ID, plus a recent photo with a plain background.
Fill in the application on the Department of Immigration portal with your dates, entry point and plan for each night.
Pay the Sustainable Development Fee online for every night you will spend in Bhutan.
Download and print the approved permit; keep a copy on your phone as well.
Carry the original document you applied with, because officers check it against the permit at the border.

sections.heading: Route permit for Punakha and beyond
paras: The Entry Permit covers Thimphu and Paro. To go further, to Punakha, Wangdue Phodrang, Phobjikha, Haa, Trongsa, Bumthang or Gasa, you have needed a separate Route Permit. It is issued by the Immigration office in Thimphu on working days, Monday to Friday. In practice your guide or tour operator takes your documents in and collects it, often while you are at the Memorial Chorten or Buddha Dordenma.

Plan your route so that you reach Thimphu on a weekday. If you arrive on a Friday evening and want to leave for Punakha on Saturday morning, the permit may not be ready. Reports in 2026 suggest the route permit process is being simplified, so check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: SDF: ₹1,200 a night, and what kids pay
paras: The Sustainable Development Fee, or SDF, is a per-night charge that goes to the government of Bhutan for conservation, health, education and infrastructure. For Indian nationals it is ₹1,200 (Nu 1,200) per person per night. Children aged 6 to 12 pay half, and children under 6 pay nothing. You pay it online with the permit or at the entry point.

For a family of two adults and two children aged 9 and 4 on a six-night trip, the SDF works out to ₹14,400 for the adults, ₹3,600 for the older child and nothing for the younger one: ₹18,000 in all. It is charged per night, not per day, so a trip that enters in the morning and leaves the next evening is one night of SDF. Check current status before you travel, because the fee has changed before.

SDF does not cover anything you use directly. Your hotel, guide, car, meals and monument tickets are all extra. When an operator quotes a package price, ask whether SDF is included, because some quotes leave it out to look cheaper. On a six-night trip for a couple, that difference is ₹14,400.

sections.heading: The 24-hour Phuentsholing waiver
paras: If you only want to cross the gate at Jaigaon, walk around Phuentsholing, eat ema datshi and buy a few things, you do not pay SDF. Casual visitors to the border towns of Phuentsholing, Samtse, Gelephu and Samdrup Jongkhar can stay up to 24 hours without SDF, as long as they stay inside the designated zone. In Phuentsholing that means not going past the Rinchending checkpoint, about 5 km up the Thimphu highway.

From September 2026, news reports said the zone was widened to allow visits to Milarepa Lhakhang and the Pachu community ecotourism site, on an approved package with a licensed guide. The details are new and may shift, so check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Guides and private cars in 2026
paras: For years, websites said Indians could drive around Thimphu and Paro on their own. That is no longer safe advice. A Department of Tourism notification dated 8 April 2026 restated the Tourism Rules and Regulations 2024: all tourists must be accompanied by a certified, licensed guide on tours beyond the first checkpoint, which for Phuentsholing is Rinchending. That includes the drive from Paro airport to Thimphu and visits to monuments. We read this as covering Indian tourists as well. Plan on a licensed guide for the whole trip beyond Phuentsholing.

Indian private cars are allowed in with a permit from the transport authority at the border. Reports in 2026 put the fee at Nu 4,500 a day for foreign-registered vehicles, and the vehicle must be under 10 years old. You still need a guide. Indian taxis from Siliguri normally stop at Jaigaon, and you switch to a Bhutan-registered tourist vehicle. Check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Money, hotels and a final checklist
paras: The Ngultrum is pegged 1:1 to the rupee and Indian rupees are accepted widely. The Embassy of India notes that Indians may carry up to ₹25,000 in ₹500 or smaller notes; above that, carry ₹100 or smaller notes. UPI and Indian cards work in some places, but carry cash. Tourists must stay in Department of Tourism-certified hotels of 3-star and above, or in registered homestays and farmhouses.
list: Original passport or Voter ID for every adult, birth certificate for children without a passport.
Printed Entry Permit and SDF receipt, plus copies on your phone.
Four passport photos per person for route permits and any surprises.
Hotel confirmations at certified properties for every night.
Guide and vehicle booked through a licensed Bhutanese operator.
Cash in ₹500 or smaller notes within the ₹25,000 limit.

faqs.q: Can Indians enter Bhutan with an Aadhaar card
faqs.a: No. Aadhaar is not accepted for entry into Bhutan, and nor are PAN cards or driving licences. Adults need either an Indian passport valid for at least six months or an original Voter ID (EPIC) card with passport photos. Children under 18 without a passport can use their original birth certificate. We have seen travellers sent back to Jaigaon with only Aadhaar, so check your documents before you leave home and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Do Indians need a visa for Bhutan
faqs.a: No. Indian citizens do not need a visa. You need a free Entry Permit, issued online through the Department of Immigration portal or on arrival at Phuentsholing, Paro airport and the other land crossings. The permit covers Thimphu and Paro for up to 15 days. Places further east, such as Punakha and Bumthang, have needed a separate route permit. Rules have changed since 2022, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How much is the SDF for Indians in Bhutan
faqs.a: The Sustainable Development Fee for Indian nationals is ₹1,200 (Nu 1,200) per person per night. Children aged 6 to 12 pay ₹600 a night and children under 6 pay nothing. A couple on a six-night trip pays ₹14,400 in SDF. It is paid online with your permit or at the entry point, and it is charged per night spent in Bhutan. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is a guide mandatory for Indian tourists in Bhutan
faqs.a: Yes, as we read the rules in 2026. A Department of Tourism notification dated 8 April 2026 restated that all tourists must be accompanied by a certified, licensed guide beyond the first designated checkpoint, which for Phuentsholing is Rinchending. Older advice saying Indians can roam Thimphu and Paro alone is out of date. A guide costs about ₹2,000–3,000 a day, indicative 2026. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can I visit Phuentsholing without paying SDF
faqs.a: Yes. Casual visitors to Phuentsholing can stay up to 24 hours without paying SDF, provided they stay within the designated zone and do not go beyond the Rinchending checkpoint, about 5 km up the highway. You still need valid ID at the gate. Reports from 2026 say the zone now allows Milarepa Lhakhang and the Pachu ecotourism site on an approved package with a guide. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can I take my own car from India to Bhutan
faqs.a: Yes, with a permit from Bhutan's transport authority at the border. Reports in 2026 put the fee for foreign-registered vehicles at about Nu 4,500 a day, and the car must be under 10 years old. You still need a licensed guide on board beyond Rinchending. For most families, a Bhutan-registered tourist car with driver at ₹4,500–6,500 a day is simpler. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How do children travel to Bhutan without a passport
faqs.a: Indian children under 18 who do not have a passport can enter on their original birth certificate. A photocopy will not do, so carry the original and keep it safe. Children aged 6 to 12 pay half SDF, ₹600 a night, and those under 6 pay no SDF. Older teenagers who have a Voter ID can use that. Check current status before you travel, because document rules have changed before.

faqs.q: What is a route permit in Bhutan
faqs.a: A route permit lets you travel beyond Thimphu and Paro to places such as Punakha, Phobjikha, Haa, Trongsa, Bumthang and Gasa. It is issued by the Immigration office in Thimphu on working days, Monday to Friday, and your guide normally collects it for you. Arrive in Thimphu on a weekday so it is ready in time. Reports suggest the process is being simplified in 2026, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How much Indian cash can I carry to Bhutan
faqs.a: The Embassy of India in Thimphu says Indians may carry up to ₹25,000 in notes of ₹500 or smaller. Above that, carry notes of ₹100 or less. Rupees are accepted widely because the Ngultrum is pegged 1:1 to the rupee. UPI and Indian cards work in some hotels and shops, but small cafés and village stalls want cash. ATMs are available in Phuentsholing, Thimphu and Paro.
